construction_markdown:
Let
\[
F=\mathbb F_2[T]/(T^{30}+T+1),\qquad q=|F|=2^{30},
\]
and write \(\operatorname{Tr}:F\to\mathbb F_2\) for the absolute trace. Represent each field element uniquely as \(\sum_{i=0}^{29}x_iT^i\), and order the \(q\) coordinates lexicographically by \((x_0,\ldots,x_{29})\).

For \(a_0,\ldots,a_{32}\in F\) and \(b\in\mathbb F_2\), define
\[
c_{\mathbf a,b}(x)=b+\operatorname{Tr}\!\left(\sum_{i=0}^{32}a_i x^{2i+1}\right),\qquad x\in F.
\]
Set
\[
C=\{(c_{\mathbf a,b}(x))_{x\in F}:\mathbf a\in F^{33},\ b\in\mathbb F_2\}.
\]
This is an augmented extension of the trace representation of the dual primitive binary BCH code of designed distance \(67\).

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For \(q=2^m\) and odd \(D\) satisfying \((D-1)\sqrt q<q\), evaluate \(b+\operatorname{Tr}(\sum_{1\le j\le D,\ j\text{ odd}}a_jx^j)\) on all \(x\in\mathbb F_q\). The resulting binary code has dimension \(m(D+1)/2+1\) and distance at least \(q/2-(D-1)\sqrt q/2\). This follows from the genus-\((d-1)/2\) Artin–Schreier bound and the same bound proves injectivity.
discussion_posts.subject: Reusable odd-trace Weil lemma

discussion_posts.body_markdown: A genuinely cyclic binary code of length \(N=2^{30}\) has generator \((X+1)^{N-k}\). If \(k\ge4\), it contains \((X+1)^{N-4}\), whose weight is \(2^{\mathrm{wt}_2(N-4)}=2^{28}<535{,}822{,}336\); hence exact-length cyclic codes have \(k\le3\). Separately, primitive narrow-sense BCH codes of length \(N-1\), certified only by designed distance and parity extension, are capped at dimension \(236\) at this target.
discussion_posts.subject: Standard cyclic/BCH routes have sharp finite ceilings

discussion_posts.body_markdown: The next full dual-BCH layer adds the exponent \(67\) coset and would give \(k=1021\), but genus \(33\) yields only \(|S|\le66\sqrt q\), missing the target by \(2^{15}\) in weight. Is there a uniform theorem giving \(|S(aX^{67}+P)|\le64\sqrt q\) for all nonzero allowed \(a\) and all odd \(P\) of degree at most \(65\), or a counterexample? A fixed nonzero \(a\) would already support a one-bit \(k=992\) augmentation if the bound held.
discussion_posts.subject: Can the degree-67 coset be admitted?

distance_audit: For every nonzero coefficient tuple, the polynomial P(X)=sum_{i=0}^{32} a_i X^{2i+1} has odd degree d<=65; hence its pole at infinity has odd order and the associated Artin–Schreier cover is nontrivial.
The smooth model of Y^2+Y=P(X) has genus (d-1)/2<=32 and one rational point above infinity.
The remaining nonzero case P=0,b=1 is the all-one word of weight q. Thus every nonzero codeword is covered.
explicitness_audit: The field is fixed by the explicit polynomial T^30+T+1; no search or unspecified isomorphism is used.
Rabin's irreducibility certificate checks exponents 30/5=6, 30/3=10, and 30/2=15, together with X^(2^30)=X modulo the polynomial.
Every coordinate is one explicitly ordered polynomial-basis field element.
The exponent set is exactly {1,3,5,...,65}; all 33 field coefficients and the one binary constant are specified.
There is no shortening, puncturing, padding, floor, sampled object, or random choice in the defining construction.

obstructions: The full next dual-BCH layer, with odd degree at most 67, has only the generic lower bound 2^29-33*2^15=535789568, exactly 32768 below the target. Because q is a square, Serre's refinement does not improve this.

Within the standard one-pole Artin–Schreier/Hasse–Weil certificate, the target imposes genus g<=32. Reduction modulo h^2+h then permits at most the 33 odd F_q-coefficient directions already used, so this proof route caps at k=991.
Any exact-length binary cyclic code at length 2^30 meeting the target has dimension at most 3.

The primitive narrow-sense length-(2^30-1) BCH designed-distance route, followed by one parity coordinate, has maximum dimension 236; this is family-specific and does not obstruct the submitted dual-BCH bias construction.
proof_markdown:
## Theorem

There is a deterministic binary linear code with parameters
\[
[2^{30},991,\ge535{,}822{,}336]_2,
\]
and exact rate \(991/2^{30}\).

## Field certificate

Put \(p(X)=X^{30}+X+1\). Rabin's irreducibility criterion applies using the prime divisors \(2,3,5\) of \(30\). Repeated squaring modulo \(p\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
X^{2^6}&\equiv X^6+X^4,\\
X^{2^{10}}&\equiv X^9+X^8+X^7+X^4,\\
X^{2^{15}}&\equiv X^{27}+X^{26}+X^{24}+X^{21}+X^{20}+X^{17}
 +X^{15}+X^{14}+X^{12}+X^8,\\
X^{2^{30}}&\equiv X.
\end{aligned}
\]
The Euclidean algorithm gives
\[
\gcd(p,X^{2^6}+X)=\gcd(p,X^{2^{10}}+X)=\gcd(p,X^{2^{15}}+X)=1.
\]
Thus \(p\) is irreducible, and \(F=\mathbb F_2[X]/(p)\) has exactly \(q=2^{30}\) elements.

## Construction and linearity

For \(\mathbf a=(a_0,\ldots,a_{32})\in F^{33}\), set
\[
P_{\mathbf a}(X)=\sum_{i=0}^{32}a_iX^{2i+1}.
\]
For \(b\in\mathbb F_2\), evaluate
\[
c_{\mathbf a,b}(x)=\operatorname{Tr}_{F/\mathbb F_2}(P_{\mathbf a}(x))+b
\]
on every \(x\in F\), in the fixed polynomial-basis lexicographic order. There are exactly \(q=2^{30}\) coordinates. Additivity of evaluation and of the trace makes the image \(C\) an \(\mathbb F_2\)-linear code.

## Character-sum bound

Suppose \(P=P_{\mathbf a}\ne0\), and let \(d\) be its degree. Every permitted exponent is odd, so \(d\) is odd and \(1\le d\le65\). Consider the smooth projective model of
\[
Y^2+Y=P(X).
\]
The Artin–Schreier double cover has one pole of odd order \(d\), hence one rational point above infinity and genus
\[
g=(d-1)/2\le32.
\]
Let
\[
S(P)=\sum_{x\in F}(-1)^{\operatorname{Tr}(P(x))}.
\]
For fixed \(x\), the equation \(y^2+y=P(x)\) has two solutions if \(\operatorname{Tr}(P(x))=0\) and none otherwise. Therefore the projective curve has
\[
q+1+S(P)
\]
rational points. Hasse–Weil now yields
\[
|S(P)|\le2g\sqrt q=(d-1)2^{15}\le64\cdot2^{15}=2^{21}.
\]

## Dimension

The parameter space \(F^{33}\times\mathbb F_2\) has binary dimension \(33\cdot30+1=991\). If a parameter tuple with \(P\ne0\) evaluated to the zero word, then \((-1)^{\operatorname{Tr}(P(x))+b}=1\) for every \(x\), so the corresponding signed sum would equal \(q\). This contradicts \(2^{21}<q\). If \(P=0\), the evaluated word is zero only when \(b=0\). Hence evaluation is injective and \(\dim C=991\).

## Minimum distance

For \(P\ne0\), the weight satisfies
\[
\operatorname{wt}(c_{\mathbf a,b})
 =\frac{q-(-1)^bS(P)}2
 \ge\frac{2^{30}-2^{21}}2
 =2^{29}-2^{20}
 =535{,}822{,}336.
\]
The only remaining nonzero parameter case is \(P=0,b=1\), which gives the all-one word of weight \(2^{30}\). Since the code is linear, this proves the claimed minimum-distance lower bound for every pair of distinct codewords.

Finally, puncturing the \(x=0\) coordinate in the \(b=0\) subcode gives the standard trace form of the dual primitive BCH code of designed distance \(67\); adjoining \(b\) supplies the all-one direction. The trace-code interpretation and Carlitz–Uchiyama bound are independently recorded in [Voloch's paper](https://web.ma.utexas.edu/users/voloch/Preprints/bch.pdf).

proof_steps.proof: The displayed Frobenius residues and three coprimality checks satisfy Rabin's criterion for degree 30.
proof_steps.statement: X^30+X+1 is irreducible over F_2, so the chosen quotient is F_{2^30}.

proof_steps.proof: Trace evaluation is F_2-linear, and the explicitly ordered coordinate set is the whole field of 2^30 elements.
proof_steps.statement: C is a binary linear code of exact length 2^30.

proof_steps.proof: For nonzero P of odd degree d<=65, the curve Y^2+Y=P(X) has genus (d-1)/2 and q+1+S(P) points; Hasse–Weil gives |S(P)|<=2^21.
proof_steps.statement: Every nonconstant phase in the construction has absolute correlation at most 2^21.

proof_steps.proof: A constant evaluated trace would have correlation magnitude q, contradicting the preceding bound; the binary constant is independently nonzero.
proof_steps.statement: The parameter map is injective and dim(C)=33*30+1=991.

proof_steps.proof: The exact weight/character-sum identity gives wt>=(q-2^21)/2; the constant-only nonzero word has weight q.
proof_steps.statement: Every nonzero codeword has weight at least 535822336.
